evals.prompt: Site's been upgraded to v17 and I'm working through the tag helper updates. Need to migrate all our `<our-img>`, `<our-link>`, and `<our-rich-text>` tags. Is it just a find/replace or is there more to it? Also noticed `@Umbraco.GetDictionaryValue` is everywhere in our views — does that need updating too?
evals.expected_output: Confirms tag helper renames are a regex find/replace (provides one), but flags two extra considerations: `<etch-cms-img>` sizing parameters changed in v17 so don't migrate from memory, and the `OurIMG` config key in appsettings.json must NOT be renamed despite the tag rename. Confirms `GetDictionaryValue` should become `GetDictionaryValueOrDefault` — explains the behaviour change (v17 returns the literal key instead of empty when missing, which renders verbatim on the page). Recommends doing this before any QA pass. Points to taghelpers-migration.md.
expectations: Confirms the <our-X> to <etch-cms-X> rename can be done via find/replace and provides a regex or command to do it
Flags that <etch-cms-img> sizing parameters changed in v17 — check the docs, don't migrate from memory
States that the OurIMG config key in appsettings.json must NOT be renamed despite the tag rename
States that @Umbraco.GetDictionaryValue should be replaced with @Umbraco.GetDictionaryValueOrDefault
Explains the behaviour change: v17 returns the literal key (not empty string) when the key is missing, causing it to render verbatim on the page
References taghelpers-migration.md

evals.prompt: QA on our v17 upgrade has raised about 40 'missing content' bugs. Looking at them, loads of pages are showing strings like `footer.copyright` and `nav.skipToContent` where the text should be. The dictionary items exist in the backoffice for most of them. Nothing was changed in the views. What's going on?
evals.expected_output: Identifies this as the GetDictionaryValue behaviour change in v17: when a key is missing or its value is empty, it now returns the literal key instead of an empty string, so keys render verbatim on the page. Fix is a project-wide replace of @Umbraco.GetDictionaryValue("key") with @Umbraco.GetDictionaryValueOrDefault("key", fallback). Notes that many of the QA bugs are likely false positives caused by this and recommends doing the replace before re-running QA. Points to taghelpers-migration.md.
expectations: Identifies the cause as v17 GetDictionaryValue returning the literal key (not an empty string) when the value is missing or empty
Provides the fix: replace @Umbraco.GetDictionaryValue with @Umbraco.GetDictionaryValueOrDefault project-wide, with a fallback value
Notes many of the QA 'missing content' reports are likely false positives from this change and recommends fixing it before re-running QA
References taghelpers-migration.md

evals.prompt: Since upgrading to v17, any page where we've put a Section block inside another Section block has a broken layout on the live site — there seem to be extra wrapper divs and the inner section's content is squashed. Top-level sections look fine. It's only on the frontend, the backoffice preview is OK.
evals.expected_output: Identifies this as the known v17 nested-section BlockGrid frontend bug. The fix is in Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/SectionContent.cshtml — bring across the delta from the v17 Etch.Cms template's version of the file (typically a conditional that skips outer-wrapper rendering when already inside a section). Advises copying from the template rather than recreating the fix from memory. Points to views-and-csp.md.
expectations: Identifies this as the v17 nested-section BlockGrid frontend rendering bug
States the fix is in Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/SectionContent.cshtml
Advises copying the change from the v17 Etch.Cms template's SectionContent.cshtml rather than recreating it from memory
References views-and-csp.md

evals.prompt: We customised a few of the Umbraco Forms templates on the v13 site (extra wrapper classes, a custom date field partial, and some JS that hooks onto field class names). Now we're on v17 — can I just copy our v13 Forms views across?
evals.expected_output: No — the v13 templates will break against v17 Forms, and overwriting the v17 templates loses customisations. The correct direction is to take the v17 stock templates and re-apply each v13 customisation to them, not the other way round. Specific watch points: wrapper classes are easy to re-add; the custom date field partial may need rewriting if the v17 field type interface or @model changed; JS hooks need the class names verifying since some changed in v17. Recommends end-to-end verification including validation, submission, reCAPTCHA and the Entries view. Points to umbraco-forms.md.
expectations: Says not to copy the v13 templates across as-is because they break against v17 Forms
Recommends starting from the v17 stock templates and re-applying each customisation to them (not applying v17 changes to the v13 versions)
Flags that the custom field type partial may need rewriting if the v17 field type interface or @model changed
Flags that JavaScript hooks tied to class names need checking because some class names changed in v17
References umbraco-forms.md

evals.prompt: I'm tidying up the CSP in Program.cs on our v17 site and want to drop 'unsafe-inline' from style-src — it looks like a leftover. Anything I should know before I remove it?
evals.expected_output: Warns that 'unsafe-inline' in style-src is required for the CIVIC Cookie Control widget; removing it breaks the cookie banner. Recommends keeping it and keeping (or adding) the inline comment explaining why. Tightening further would require moving CIVIC styles into a CSP-friendly configuration, which is a separate piece of work. Points to views-and-csp.md and/or the backend skill's program-cs-v17.md.
expectations: Warns that style-src 'unsafe-inline' is required for the CIVIC cookie banner and removing it will break it
Recommends keeping the inline comment that explains why UnsafeInline is there
Notes that removing it safely would need CIVIC styles moved to a CSP-friendly configuration, as separate work
References views-and-csp.md or program-cs-v17.md
